orchestrator_feedback: The ideality factor of 2.05 strongly suggests recombination-dominated transport rather than pure thermionic emission, yet all barrier-based models failed with unreasonable barrier heights (phi_B=0.726 eV, phi_TAT=0.176 eV) indicating these mechanisms are inappropriate for this ZnO-Au system. Avoid Schottky/thermionic emission models and trap-assisted tunneling since the log-scale fits (R²_log ~0.89) capture curvature but yield physically meaningless parameters, particularly the n=3.79 extracted from thermionic fits which far exceeds recombination limits. The SCLC and Poole-Frenkel models showed poor fits (R²_log=0.64 and -1.12 respectively), ruling out bulk-limited conduction mechanisms. Instead, try equivalent circuits combining multiple parallel conduction paths: a recombination current component (exponential with n≈2) plus either a defect-assisted hopping term or grain boundary-limited transport model, since polycrystalline ZnO often exhibits such mixed conduction. The substantial current density at zero bias (J₀=1.14×10⁻⁶ A/cm²) and near-ideal n=2.05 point toward interface recombination centers rather than bulk or injection-limited processes, so focus on interface state recombination models with explicit series resistance.
